title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months of His Life to Become Parashurama. No Other Film. No Distractions.
excerpt: The actor will undergo six months of physical transformation before a single frame is shot for Amar Kaushik's mythological epic Mahavatar. Shraddha Kapoor is in talks to star opposite him.
body:
There is ambitious, and then there is what **Vicky Kaushal** is about to do.

The actor has carved out an 18-month window — June 2026 through December 2027 — exclusively for **Mahavatar**, Maddock Films' mythological action epic in which he will play **Chiranjeevi Parashurama**, the immortal warrior-sage and sixth avatar of Vishnu. During this stretch, Kaushal will not take on a single other film. No quick cameos. No brand commitments. Just one role, consumed totally.

It is, by any measure, the most extreme commitment a mainstream Bollywood actor has made to a single project in recent memory.

## The Transformation Begins

The timeline is staggering. As soon as Kaushal wraps **Sanjay Leela Bhansali's** *Love and War* — the long-awaited drama that reunites him with **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Alia Bhatt**, currently in its final 50-day schedule and targeting a January 21, 2027 release — he will enter a six-month preparatory module designed by director **Amar Kaushik**.

> "The prep is going on for 6-7 months. We have worked on the set design, weapon design, how every character would look. The scripting is done. Yet, we need more time." — Amar Kaushik

The programme is not just about packing on muscle, though Kaushal's physical transformation will be central. Kaushik has designed a regimen that includes intensive acting workshops, movement training, and deep psychological preparation for a character who occupies a singular place in Hindu mythology — an immortal sage who carries an axe and walks the earth across yugas, destined to emerge again at the end of the Kali Yuga as the guru of Kalki, Vishnu's final avatar.

This is not a costume drama. This is world-building on a scale Bollywood rarely attempts.

## A Fresh Pairing

The other headline: **Shraddha Kapoor** is reportedly in advanced talks to play the female lead. According to Mid-Day, the makers consider her the primary choice, and if she signs on, this will be her first collaboration with Kaushal — a pairing that has never appeared on screen before.

The combination is intriguing. Shraddha, who delivered back-to-back blockbusters with *Stree 2* (which Kaushik also directed), brings a box-office pull that is undeniable. Kaushal, who has proven he can carry spectacle and intimacy with equal force — from *Uri* to *Sam Bahadur* to his turn in Bhansali's universe — brings the kind of intensity a mythological epic demands.

If the deal closes, Mahavatar will pair two of Maddock Films' biggest stars in a project that could redefine the studio's ambitions.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who have watched the Indian film industry chase the mythology space with mixed results — from *Adipurush*'s VFX debacle to *Brahmastra*'s polarising reception to *Kalki 2898 AD*'s ambitious scope — Mahavatar represents something different. The preparation time alone signals that this is not a rush job. Kaushik, who turned *Stree* from a sleeper hit into a franchise-defining phenomenon and then tripled down with *Stree 2*, understands how to blend Indian mythology with commercial filmmaking without losing the soul of either.

The production has been in pre-production for over seven months already. Set design, weapon design, costume design, and character look-books are complete. The scripting is locked. What remains is Vicky Kaushal himself — the physical vessel through which Parashurama will be brought to life.

## The Bigger Picture

The timing is significant. While Kaushal locks himself into Mahavatar, **Ranveer Singh** has acquired the rights to Amish Tripathi's *The Immortals of Meluha* and is preparing to play Lord Shiva in a separate mythological franchise. Bollywood's biggest leading men are no longer fighting over the same rom-com scripts. They are racing to build cinematic mythologies that can compete on a global stage.

Mahavatar does not yet have a confirmed release date, though Independence Day 2027 is being discussed. If that pans out, Maddock's other tentpole, *Stree 3*, would likely shift to accommodate it.

For now, the message from Vicky Kaushal's camp is clear: this is not a film. It is an era.
